previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, mechanical aortic valve replacement, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for chest pain and shortness of breath. Her symptoms were attributed to a type II non-ST elevation myocardial infarction in the setting of fluid overload and demand ischemia. Troponins were mildly elevated but stable, with no acute EKG changes. She underwent hemodialysis, which improved her respiratory symptoms. Her INR was supratherapeutic, likely due to interaction with levofloxacin, so warfarin was held during admission. She was discharged home with services after clinical improvement, with instructions to follow up on INR testing, restart warfarin based on results, and use nitroglycerin for any recurrent chest pain.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with left hand steal syndrome status post banding
of brachiocepahlic fistula yesterday with only slight improvement in hand
numbness. 

COMPARISON:  Fistulogram ___.  

Exam:  Duplex and color Doppler imaging of the left upper extremity arterial
system 

FINDINGS:

Patent subclavian, axillary and brachial arteries. 

Velocities are :  242 centimeters/second in the subclavian artery, 240
centimeters/second in the axillary artery, 270 centimeters/second in the right
brachial artery proximally and 268 centimeters/second in the right brachial
artery distally. Values are expectedly high given the presence of an AV
fistula .
Velocity in the proximal radial artery is 22 centimeters/second, 21
centimeters/second in the mid radial artery and 49 centimeters/second in the
distal radial artery.  

In normal triphasic waveform is seen distally in the wrist, but the waveform
is diminished and velocities are decreased in the mid forearm.  

Grayscale imaging reveals a minimal amount of calcified plaque in the left
axillary artery.  

IMPRESSION:

1. The radial artery is patent, however flow is significantly diminished in
the forearm, but improved at the wrist.  

2.  The subclavian, axillary and brachial arteries are patent without evidence
of high-grade stenosis.

INDICATION:  ___ female with left upper extremity AV fistula steal. 
Please map lower extremity veins for conduit.

FINDINGS:

RIGHT:  The right greater saphenous vein is patent with diameters of 2-2.6 mm
below the knee.  The diameters above the knee range from 2.5-5.2 mm.

The small saphenous vein is patent with small diameters all less than 2 mm.

LEFT LEG:  The left greater saphenous vein has been previously harvested.  The
left small saphenous vein is diminutive with diameters of 1 mm or less.

IMPRESSION:  Patent right greater saphenous vein and small lesser saphenous
veins bilaterally.

INDICATION:  ___ female with left upper extremity AV fistula and steal
syndrome.  Please map right upper extremity for new fistula.

Right upper extremity vein mapping was performed.

Cephalic vein:  The cephalic vein wrist measures 3 mm.  In the mid upper
forearm it is small measuring 1.3-1.7 mm.  The upper arm cephalic diameters
are 3.4, 4.0, 4.0 mm.
Basilic:  The forearm basilic vein ranges in size from 1.7-3.0 mm.  The upper
arm basilic diameters are 0, 3.0, 4.0 mm respectively.

The central subclavian vein waveform has normal cardiac and respiratory
phasicity.  The basilic artery has triphasic waveforms with diameter of 0.4
cm.  The radial artery is patent with triphasic waveforms and has a diameter
of 1.5 mm.

IMPRESSION:  Patent cephalic and basilic veins with variable diameters as
noted.  Patent central veins.  Singular brachial arteries and small radial
artery without significant calcifications.

INDICATION:  Left upper extremity fistula undergoing revision. Preoperative
study.  

COMPARISON:  CXR ___, CT ___

FRONTAL AND LATERAL CHEST:  There is no focal consolidation or pneumothorax.
Pleural effusions have resolved on the right and substantially improved on the
left with tiny residual left pleural effusion. Cardiomegaly is unchanged.
Patient is status post aortic valve replcement.

IMPRESSION:  No pneumonia or edema.
